title: A Leavers' Celebration
strapline: Off to big school — look how far you've grown, and off you go.
intent: Marking the move on to school helps children look back with pride and forward with confidence and excitement.
Celebrating how much they've grown and learned builds self-esteem and a strong sense of their own journey.
Talking about starting school, with all its hopes and worries, helps children name feelings and feel ready.
Remembering their time here — friends, favourite play, milestones — honours belonging and gives a gentle goodbye.
The celebration turns a big transition into something warm, proud and hopeful, not frightening.
implementation: Gather memories of each child's time here — photos, favourite moments, things they can do now — into a keepsake or memory book.
Celebrate their growth openly: 'Look at everything you can do now — you're so ready for school.'
Talk about big school warmly, welcoming both excitement and worry: 'What are you looking forward to? Is anything a bit wobbly?'
Play out school in role-play — a classroom, a uniform, a lunchbox — so it feels familiar and exciting.
Hold a proper goodbye — a celebration, a song, a keepsake to take with them — so leaving is honoured.
Follow the children — some will want to talk about school endlessly, others will need reassurance it's okay to feel unsure.
key_questions: What are you most looking forward to about big school?
What can you do now that you couldn't when you started here?
Is anything about school feeling a bit wobbly?
What has been your favourite thing about being here?
What would you like to remember about your time with us?

impact.text: Children talk about how they've grown and what they can do now.
Children talk about starting school and name their feelings about it.
Children show confidence and readiness to take on a new step.
Children remember and value friendships and their time here.
Children play out school and rehearse the new routines.

enhancements: A memory book or keepsake of each child's time at nursery.
A big-school role-play with a classroom, uniform, lunchbox and register.
A 'look how I've grown' display from starting here to now.
A leavers' celebration with a song, certificates and a proper goodbye.
A feelings talk-time about the excitement and worries of school.

playing_exploring: Children play out big school and explore what it will be like.
They engage warmly with memories of their time here.
active_learning: Children show pride and confidence in how far they've come.
They rehearse school routines and grow ready for the step.
creating_thinking: Children reflect on their own growth and journey.
They make sense of the change ahead and how they feel about it.
